security_spec.violation_condition: In an RV32 FreeBSD kernel, M-mode firmware (OpenSBI) configures a TOR-mode PMP entry intending to grant S-mode access to the uppermost word of a 34-bit physical address space; the TOR encoding cannot represent 2^34 as a range top, so the PMP entry either fails to match the intended region or must be reconfigured using NAPOT mode instead.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: RV32 TOR PMP range top truncation at 2^34-4
security_spec.summary: FreeBSD S-mode never directly programs PMP CSRs (M-mode only), but must be aware that on RV32 with 34-bit phys, OpenSBI-set TOR PMP entries silently cannot cover the uppermost 4 bytes of physical memory — the kernel's pmap would see those pages as permanently inaccessible to S-mode unless firmware uses NAPOT instead.

findings.finding: FreeBSD RISC-V kernel does not configure PMP entries directly. PMP is managed entirely by M-mode firmware (OpenSBI). The kernel's only PMP interaction is efi_exclude_sbi_pmp_cb() at machdep.c:542-606, which works around OpenSBI's first PMP entry by excluding the protected EFI BootServicesData region from physmem. The kernel never reads or writes pmpaddr/pmpcfg CSRs. This is by design: PMP configuration is an M-mode responsibility, and FreeBSD runs in S-mode.
findings.snippet:
/*
 * OpenSBI uses the first PMP entry to prevent buggy supervisor
 * software from overwriting the firmware. However, this
 * region may not be properly marked as reserved, leading
 * to an access violation exception whenever the kernel
 * attempts to write to a page from that region.
 *
 * Fix this by excluding first EFI memory map entry
 * if it is marked as "BootServicesData".
 */
first = true;
efi_map_foreach_entry(efihdr, efi_exclude_sbi_pmp_cb, &first);

spec_citations.excerpt: It is not possible to represent the address 2^XLEN+2^ as the top of a range, so, for example, in an RV32 system with 34-bit physical addresses, a TOR PMP cannot be used to give less-privileged modes access to the uppermost word of memory. Either a NAPOT PMP can be used, or that memory can be left inaccessible to less-privileged modes.

findings.finding: FreeBSD RISC-V build is hardcoded for RV64 only: -march=rv64imafdch_zifencei. RV32 is not a supported build target in kern.mk:169 or anywhere else in the build system. The RV32 TOR PMP vulnerability pattern (inability to represent 2^34 as a TOR top) therefore cannot manifest in any FreeBSD kernel that can be produced by this build system.

MACHINE_ARCH is defined as "riscv64". Combined with kern.mk:169 hardcoding rv64 and the absence of SV32 paging support (vmparam.h:116 notes SV32 exists but is not supported), FreeBSD RISC-V is exclusively 64-bit. The 34-bit TOR PMP truncation issue is architecturally irrelevant for RV64, where PMP address registers encode 56-bit physical addresses.
